subfamily: a whiskey sour on orange: Duffy's Herald Punch (New York Herald, 1901; Imbibe! pdf 92: the juice of one rich orange [2 oz], one teaspoonful powdered sugar, one ordinary drink of rye [2 oz], St. Croix rum to flavor [1/2 oz], shaken, strained into sour glass), with the orange sharpened with citric and malic acid (two-fifths of Liquid Intelligence p. 60's correction to lime strength) so it holds as a proper sour
glass: stemmed sour glass (about 240 ml), chilled, no ice

ingredients.note: 1 1/2 teaspoons caster sugar, stirred into the juice first (Wondrich, Imbibe! pdf 92)

_status: v1.1 (Tomas, round 4; story ruled by Wren r3: Duffy, foresight, spark lead 1 alone; nothing in the glass changed since v1). Rye as a style: straight rye, 50% modelled, 43% or stronger (40% edges at 14.4% finished vs the 15.0% floor). Rum as a style: Virgin Islands (St. Croix), 40% unsourced. Juice acid window proved 2.8-3.1% (sharpened); sugar as 6 g caster sugar.
